_note: Replaces the targets.csv named in README.md — the data is too nested for CSV. Every value here was retrieved from ChEMBL, RCSB, UniProt or a cited publication. Nothing is recalled or estimated. Values that could not be retrieved are the string NOT_FOUND.
_expected_output: What a correct dossier must say. This is the grading key for the fixture run.

_measurement_definitions._why: A grading key with no stated definition drifts. Every count below was re-measured 2026-08-15 against Paperclip (sql -s proteins) with the definitions in this block. If you change a definition, re-measure the whole file — do not patch one number.
_measurement_definitions.distinct_compounds: COUNT(DISTINCT molregno) FROM chembl_v.bioactivities_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC> AND n_target_components = 1. The n_target_components=1 predicate is LOAD-BEARING and is the single most common way to get these numbers wrong — see _audit_2026_08_15.
_measurement_definitions.total_activities: COUNT(*) over the same view with the same n_target_components = 1 predicate.
_measurement_definitions.best_potency_nm: MAX(pchembl_value) over the same filtered set, converted 10^(9-pchembl), AND THEN rejected if the source assay description is uncharacterised per CLAUDE.md rule 6 ('Inhibition of X (unknown origin)', 'Binding affinity to X (unknown origin)'). Where the raw maximum is rejected on that ground the entry says so explicitly. standard_relation must be '='.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_total: COUNT(DISTINCT entry_id) FROM pdb_v.structures_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC>. NOTE: this view has one row per (accession, entry, entity), so COUNT(*) overcounts — KRAS is 534 rows for 522 entries.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_holo: structure-select SKILL.md §1 as written 2026-08-15: an entry is HOLO if it has >=1 non-polymer ligand with formula_weight BETWEEN 250 AND 1200 whose comp_id is not in the skill's $EXCL cofactor/additive list. Cofactors and cryo-EM additives are excluded BY IDENTITY, not by size. This replaced an earlier '>=300 Da, no upper bound' rule; the two rules disagree on 6 of the 11 targets here and every pre-audit holo count in this file was generated with the OLD rule.
known_limits_of_the_holo_rule: The 1200 Da CEILING drops genuine PROTAC/degrader co-crystals — BCL-2 8FY1 (YF8, 1640 Da) and 8FY2 (YFH, 1682 Da) are real bivalent BCL-2 degrader structures and are scored APO by this rule.

$EXCL is comp_id-keyed and leaks. Confirmed leaks in this file: TNF-alpha 5UUI (MTN = MTSL nitroxide spin label, 264 Da) and RORgt 4NIE (DMX = NDSB-256 sulfobetaine crystallisation additive, 257 Da). Both pass the filter and both are FALSE HOLO. Read ligand names, never comp_ids alone.
drugbank_id is not a druglikeness signal — MTN carries DB08217.
_measurement_definitions.data_validity_comment_is_NOT_usable_here: chembl_v.bioactivities_by_accession exposes a data_validity_comment column that is NULL for EVERY row, on all 11 accessions in this file, exactly like the already-documented always-NULL `modality` column. The raw chembl.activities table does carry it (345,635 'Outside typical range' rows overall; 91 on JAK1) but the VIEW does not propagate it, and the view is not pre-filtered — JAK1 returns all 48,836 raw activity_ids. Separately, JAK1's 91 flagged raw rows carry NO pchembl_value at all, so flagged rows can never be the top-potency rows. Any fixture note claiming top potencies 'were flagged Outside typical range and excluded' is describing a filter that did nothing.

_audit_2026_08_15.headline: The precedent axis is TRUSTWORTHY and does not need regeneration. The structure axis DOES — every holo count in this file was generated with a superseded rule. ChEMBL drift is not the problem and never was: all 11 compound counts and 6 of 7 activity counts re-measured EXACT.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_challenge_that_failed: JAK1 14,342 was reported as stale against a 'measured' 14,472. The fixture was RIGHT and the challenge was WRONG. 14,472 is the same view with the n_target_components = 1 predicate dropped, which pools inherited hits from multi-component targets (complexes, PPI pairs, PROTAC ternary complexes). Verified by reproducing the fixture value exactly on all eleven accessions with the predicate and the inflated value exactly on all eleven without it. Had this been blessed it would have silently corrupted six of the eleven targets.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_challenge_that_succeeded: TNF 15 -> 17 is a real DEFINITION CHANGE from the '>=300 Da' holo rule to the '250-1200 Da + $EXCL' rule. Both rules were re-run and reproduce 15 and 17 exactly. But the right answer is 16, not 17: of the two added entries, 6OOY (A7M, a real benzimidazole from an already-counted series) belongs and 5UUI (MTN = MTSL nitroxide spin label on an engineered T77C cysteine) does not.
_audit_2026_08_15.the_second_challenge_that_succeeded: JAK1 0.032 -> 0.010 nM is a FIXTURE QUERY DEFECT. The fixture excluded all IC50s as 'flagged Outside typical range'; the view never populates that column, and JAK1's genuinely-flagged raw rows carry no pchembl at all. The 0.010 nM value traces to a 2016 document, so data growth cannot explain it, and it is corroborated by 2 compounds x 2 independent assays with 60 compounds above the old value.

immunology.best_potency_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-15 — the old 0.032 nM was a FIXTURE QUERY DEFECT, not data drift. The old note claimed 'Top IC50s all flagged Outside typical range — no clean IC50 retrieved'. That is false twice over: (1) the view never populates data_validity_comment at all, so nothing was flagged for it to exclude; (2) JAK1's 91 genuinely-flagged rows in raw chembl.activities carry NO pchembl_value, so they were never in contention for the maximum. Data growth CANNOT explain this: CHEMBL3888428 is a 2016 document ('Cyanomethylpyrazole carboxamides as janus kinase inhibitors'), so a clean 0.010 nM IC50 predated the fixture by a decade.
immunology.best_potency_is_not_an_outlier: Explicitly checked, because a best-potency resting on one unreplicated row would be a bad grading key regardless of magnitude. It rests on 2 compounds x 2 independent assays at pchembl 11.00, 15 compounds at >=10.90, and 60 compounds at or above the OLD value of 0.032 nM. The top of the distribution is a dense congeneric series (N-methyl-deazapurine cyclobutyl sulfones), not a spike. The superseded 0.032 nM row (CHEMBL5828027, assay CHEMBL5736542 LanthaScreen Ki) is real and still present — it was simply never the maximum.

immunology.best_potency_note: RAISED 2026-08-15. The old 0.1 nM (CHEMBL4635823 IC50 in assay CHEMBL4623385, 'Binding affinity to recombinant human RORgammat transfected in HEK293T', confidence 9) is real, characterised and remains the best cell-context IC50 — it simply was not the maximum. The maximum is a thermal-shift-derived Kd. Both survive rule 6 (neither is an 'unknown origin' description), so the maximum governs. CAVEAT worth carrying: a 17 pM Kd from a ThermoFluor melt is an extrapolation well below what a thermal-shift assay resolves directly, and the same compound CHEMBL4635823 carries an even lower Kd of 0.003 nM in assay 1989649 that ChEMBL declines to assign a pchembl_value to at all. Sub-0.1 nM on this target should be read as 'at the biophysical floor'. The verdict is unaffected: sub-nanomolar either way.
immunology.pdb_holo_note: DEFINITION CHANGE with a KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE — read before grading. 152 was the old >=300 Da rule; 154 is the current 250-1200 Da + $EXCL rule. The 3 added entries are NOT all real: 5G44 (YTZ, 255 Da, 4-amino-N-(1,3-thiazol-2-yl)benzenesulfonamide = sulfathiazole) is a legitimate drug-like fragment; 29OB (AND, 288 Da, 3-beta-hydroxy-5-androsten-17-one = DHEA) is an ENDOGENOUS STEROL, the native-ligand class for this nuclear receptor, and is target validation rather than small-molecule precedent; 4NIE (DMX, 257 Da, 3-[benzyl(dimethyl)ammonio]propane-1-sulfonate = NDSB-256) is a NON-DETERGENT SULFOBETAINE CRYSTALLISATION ADDITIVE and is a straightforward false holo that $EXCL does not catch. 154 is the grading value because it is what the skill produces; the defensible count is 152-153. Accept 152, 153 or 154 from an agent that names the DHEA and NDSB-256 entries; the failure mode to catch is an agent that reports 154 without inspecting the three ligands.

6OOY.verdict: REAL drug-like ligand — count it. It is the des-pyridyl parent of a genuine congeneric series deposited the same day: A6Y (343 Da, 6OOZ) and A7A (424 Da, 6OP0) were ALREADY counted under the old rule. The 300 Da floor was splitting one chemical series across the holo/apo boundary.

5UUI.identity: S-[(1-oxyl-2,2,5,5-tetramethyl-2,5-dihydro-1H-pyrrol-3-yl)methyl] methanesulfonothioate = MTSL, the standard nitroxide spin label for EPR/DEER
5UUI.entry_title: Crystal Structure of Spin-Labeled T77C TNFa
5UUI.verdict: NOT a drug-like ligand — FALSE HOLO. It is a covalent biophysical probe conjugated to an ENGINEERED cysteine (the T77C mutation is in the entry title). This is the same failure class as the cryo-EM lipid additives (cholesterol hemisuccinate Y01, phosphatidylcholine) that produced a phantom holo count of 3 on CD20 where the truth was 0. Note it carries drugbank_id DB08217, which is precisely why drugbank_id must never gate holo.

slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.structure_caveat: SPD304 is a bis-electrophilic compound widely regarded as a promiscuous/cytotoxic frequent hitter. There IS a holo structure and it is exactly the misleading kind.
slot_5_precedent_structure_conflict.why_in_set: Carries THREE failure modes at once: modality trap (5 approved biologics, 0 small molecules), assay artifact (45% of bioactivity is a different target's assay), and misleading structure (holo ligand is a known frequent hitter).
